newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish markets ignore rosy government forecast.
newsitem.headline: Danish markets ignore rosy government forecast.

text.p: Danish markets on Tuesday ignored bullish finance ministry forecasts of falling budget deficits and booming growth, with analysts saying they had expected no less.

The ministry on Tuesday cut its estimates for the 1996 and 1997 state budget deficits to 28.5 billion crowns and 19.3 billion crowns respectively, from an August forecast of 31.0 billion and 22.6 billion crown shortfalls.
The bond market was more influenced by events elsewhere than at home, tracking Frankfurt -- and particularly the December Bund -- down amid lacklustre turnover.
Analysts agreed the budget news was encouraging, but said the downward revisions were of insufficient size to excite the market.
"The improvement is good news but may be too small to have an impact on Danish spreads," a bank economist said.
BG Bank Research Chief Frank Fryd Petersen said that the constant flow of positive indicators would eventually feed into the bond market.
"It will create upside pressure on spreads," he said adding the government still needed to rein in local authority spending and public building.
On the share market, the KFX top-20 index rose throughout the day but dealers said that it had been tracking foreign markets up anyway and was unaffected by the budget announcement.

"The forecasts are exactly as expected, there's no big news there. The optimistic view presented in the government's August forecast has since been confirmed by monthly indicators," an analyst said. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
